title: Power Pages: self-service site ownership transfer in the admin centre
notes: claim 55: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the controls table omits the managed-identity exception to app ownership, skips documented navigation steps, and presents an API name instead of a callable audit endpoint. The statement that transfers leave licensing unchanged also lacks Microsoft documentation, although the roadmap details and main transfer procedure are supported.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Power Pages supports secure ownership transfer for eligible sites without requiring a support request.
claims.quote: Power Pages now supports secure site ownership transfer for eligible sites. Existing site owners and global administrators can assign ownership to another valid user within the tenant without requiring manual intervention from support.

claims.quote: Your organization needs a reliable way to transfer ownership of Power Pages sites when responsibilities change due to team reassignments, role changes, or employee departures.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: transfer row
claims.claim: The transfer setting is in Power Platform admin center under Manage > Power Pages > site > Site Details > Edit > Owner.
claims.quote: select Manage, and then select Power Pages. ... Select the Power Pages site ... On the Site Details page, select Edit. ... In the Owner field, remove the current owner and search for the new owner.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: transfer automation gap

claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages ownership transfer API; Power Pages ownership transfer PowerShell bulk. Opened learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/admin/transfer-ownership and admin-roles; checked Set-AdminPowerAppOwner search excerpts. No site-transfer call found.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: audit row
claims.claim: Power Pages activity logs are accessible in Microsoft Purview portal through Solutions > Audit.
claims.quote: On the left navigation pane, select Solutions and then select Audit.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: audit API cell
claims.claim: Office 365 Management API (Power Pages activity logs; operation OwnershipTransferred) is the REST call for retrieving the transfer audit trail.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages ownership transfer API. Opened activity-logs-power-pages and office-365-management-activity-api-reference. The cited page confirms API access but this cell supplies neither an HTTP method nor a versioned endpoint.
claims.fix: Replace the descriptive API name with a documented method and endpoint, for example GET https://manage.office.com/api/v1.0/{tenant_id}/activity/feed/subscriptions/content?contentType=Audit.General, and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office/office-365-management-api/office-365-management-activity-api-reference. Explain that this lists available content for an active subscription; retrieve the returned contentUri and filter retrieved records for OwnershipTransferred.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Ownership transfers are searchable as Transfer site ownership with operation OwnershipTransferred in Purview.
claims.quote: Transfer site ownership | OwnershipTransferred | Ownership of the site is transferred to another user.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Auditing must be configured and enabled for the Power Platform production environments to monitor.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls: app-owner UI cell
claims.claim: The Azure portal path is Microsoft Entra ID > App registrations > Portals-<website name> > Owners > Add owners.
claims.quote: Under Manage, select App registrations. ... Select the website app ... This application is called Portals-<<website name>>. ... Under Manage, select Owners. ... Select Add owners.
claims.fix: Use Microsoft Entra ID > Manage > App registrations > website app > Manage > Owners > Add owners, followed by selecting a user and Select. Explain the documented Portals-<<website name>> naming separately. Repair the rendered cell's split placeholder and extra separator. The pre-check's missing placeholder is cosmetic; the omitted Manage sections are not.

claims.where: controls[3]; Scope: Rollout; Governance controls: tenant-switch gap
claims.claim: No tenant-wide UI or API switch to disable site ownership transfer is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages ownership transfer disable approval. Opened learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/admin/transfer-ownership, admin-roles and manage-administrative-access-with-rbac. No tenant-disable UI setting or API found.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Governance controls: final paragraph
claims.claim: Access to transfer is limited only by the required roles.

claims.fix: Replace 'Access is limited only by the required roles' and 'access control only through the required roles' with 'Transfers follow the documented role, app-ownership and recipient prerequisites; sites using Power Platform managed identity do not require app ownership.'

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not document transfer notifications or notification controls.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages ownership transfer notifications. Opened learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/admin/transfer-ownership and admin-roles; checked the activity-logs-power-pages page. No notification behaviour or notification setting found.

claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Power Advisor ownerless sites recommendations performance operational efficiency. Read all Sites entries at learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/performance-recommendations and operational-efficiency-recommendations. No ownerless-site recommendation listed.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: No automated or bulk ownership transfer is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages ownership transfer PowerShell bulk; Power Pages ownership transfer API. Opened transfer-ownership and admin-roles; inspected PowerShell search excerpts. Only the interactive, single-site transfer procedure was found.

claims.where: Governance controls: final paragraph
claims.claim: No approval step for site ownership transfer is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages ownership transfer disable approval. Opened learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/admin/transfer-ownership and admin-roles. The documented workflow ends with the initiating admin selecting Save and Transfer; no separate approval control found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Feature-specific licensing, metering and charges for ownership transfer are not published, so the licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages ownership transfer license charge; Power Pages transfer ownership licensing charge meter capacity authenticated anonymous users per website month. Read transfer-ownership and Power Pages licensing FAQ excerpts. No transfer-specific licence, meter or fee found.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The transfer page's prerequisites list roles, admin-center access and an enabled Entra Member user, without naming a licence or charge.
claims.quote: You are the website app owner and have any one of the following roles ... You have access to the Power Platform admin center. ... The new owner is an enabled Microsoft Entra user with a Member user type.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Pages licensing is capacity-based, using authenticated and anonymous users per website per month.
claims.quote: Power Pages (formerly Power Apps portals) licensing is capacity based and offers two types of capacities based on user type: Authenticated users per website/month and Anonymous users per website/month.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: final clause
claims.claim: A transfer does not change which site is licensed.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages transfer ownership licensing charge meter capacity; Power Pages transfer ownership licensing unchanged. Read transfer-ownership and Power Pages licensing FAQ excerpts. Neither states the licensing consequences of an ownership transfer.
claims.fix: Remove 'a transfer does not change which site is licensed'. Retain the sourced product-level capacity explanation and the statement that transfer-specific licensing is not yet published.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Purview audit retention
claims.claim: Keeping the transfer audit events can involve Purview retention licensing costs.
claims.quote: To retain audit logs for 10 years, the user who generates the audit log must also have a 10-year audit log retention add-on license in addition to an E5 license.
claims.fix: Clarify that extended retention can require additional licensing, rather than implying all retention costs extra, and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-retention-policies and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-solutions-overview. The latter documents default retention without buying a long-term retention add-on.

claims.where: Governance controls: Set-AdminPowerAppOwner paragraph
claims.claim: Set-AdminPowerAppOwner exists and is documented for canvas app ownership, not Power Pages site transfer.
claims.quote: Set logged in user as the owner of a canvas app ... Set-AdminPowerAppOwner -AppName 'AppName' -AppOwner $Global:currentSession.userId -EnvironmentName 'EnvironmentName'
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/powerapps-powershell#power-apps-commands to sources for the canvas-app distinction.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout, inventory bullet
claims.claim: Power Platform admin center inventory can be filtered to sites and by owner to review a user's Power Pages sites.
claims.quote: Filtering the Item type column to sites limits the grid to Power Pages sites. ... For example, filter by environment to review sites in a specific environment, by owner to review a user's sites

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout, inventory preview qualification
claims.claim: Power Pages inventory is documented as preview.
claims.quote: This feature is in preview. ... This feature is being rolled out gradually across regions and might not be available yet in your region.
claims.fix: Keep the preview qualification and add that regional rollout is gradual and the view might not yet be available in the reader's region.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout, new-owner access check
claims.claim: Microsoft advises verifying that the new owner can access and manage the site.
claims.quote: Verify that the new owner can access and manage the site.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: An ownership transfer does not move site data and stays inside existing data boundaries.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages transfer ownership data visitors. Read learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/admin/transfer-ownership; inspected migration and security search results. The feature page describes ownership and access effects, not a guarantee about data movement or boundaries.
claims.fix: Remove 'it does not move site data' and the unsourced data-boundary assertion from the rationale. Explain the low-risk judgement using the documented deliberate admin action and required permissions instead.

claims.where: rationale: impact
claims.claim: Visitors to the site are not affected by the transfer feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages transfer ownership data visitors. Read learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/admin/transfer-ownership and its permissions caveat. No passage guarantees that visitors are unaffected.
claims.fix: Remove the assurance that visitors are unaffected. Keep low impact as the wiki's judgement that the documented workflow is aimed at administrators and the owners involved.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The documented transfer workflow requires an administrator to choose a site, a new owner and confirm the transfer.
claims.quote: Select the Power Pages site that you want to update. ... Select the new owner, and then select Save. ... Review the confirmation message, and then select Transfer.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The controls table includes the inventory control that the governance checklist tells administrators to use.
claims.quote: Use the Power Platform admin center inventory, filtered to sites and by owner ... [The table has transfer, audit search, app ownership and tenant-disable rows, but no inventory row.]
claims.fix: Add an inventory row with scope tenant, the preview and gradual-rollout qualifications, and UI Power Platform admin center > Manage > Inventory > Item type: sites; filter by owner. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/admin/power-pages-inventory.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The controls table includes the auditing-enablement control that the governance checklist tells administrators to configure.
claims.quote: Turn on auditing for the production environments that host Power Pages sites ... [The audit row instead leads to Purview Solutions > Audit for reading logs.]
claims.fix: Add a separate environment-scoped auditing-enablement row. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/activity-logging-auditing/activity-logs-overview and give its documented Manage > Environments > production environment > Settings > Product > Privacy and Security > Storage Shared Access Signature (SAS) Security Settings > Enable SAS Logging in Purview path, with the auditing and licensing prerequisites.

claims.where: Governance controls: final paragraph and table
claims.claim: The controls table records the approval-control gap stated in the prose.
claims.quote: There is ... no documented approval step. [The table has a tenant-disable gap, but no approval-control gap.]
claims.fix: Add a separate approval-workflow control row with both UI and API null and a note that Microsoft documents no separate approval workflow as of November 2026.
